column1: # Why measures: a first-order continuous-time delta-sigma modulator clocked
# at 5 MHz, sampling a 13 kHz 0.3 V sine for 5 ms (24,999 decisions). The
# reference's own bitstream has not converged at the deck step. ngspice-46 at
# .tran 0.01u (10 ns ceiling) and at 10x refinement (1 ns) place every edge
# within 0.65 ns of each other up to clock 258; from there 3,034 of the
# 24,999 bits differ. Between 10x and 40x refinement (first 0.5 ms) only 2
# of 2,499 bits differ, the first at clock 2,287. RSpice at the deck step
# follows the refined reference far longer than the deck-step reference does:
#   pair (5 ms, bit sampled 100 ns after each clock)   first differing bit   bits differing
#   RSpice deck step vs ngspice deck step                     258                 2,868
# A pointwise comparison samples single bits, so it measures where each run's
# bitstream wandered, not the modulator. The gates measure what the deck is
# for, the digit density following the input, plus the early edges, where
# every decision still agrees, and the integrator swing.
# The stored table keeps 1,001 of ngspice's 1.3 million rows, one per 25
# clocks, too sparse to resolve an edge or a half-period mean, so every gate
# carries ref=: the value measured from ngspice-46 at the deck step at full
# resolution (.tran 0.01u 5m, trapezoidal, every accepted point). Each
# tolerance is twice the larger of ngspice's own movement under 10x
# refinement and RSpice's deviation from ref=, taken over the whole family
# (every edge or window of it in a full-resolution RSpice run, and the gate
#   family                               ngspice 10x moves   RSpice deviates   tolerance
# A flipped early decision moves the n-th crossing by a whole 200 ns clock.
# The half-period windows follow the input's sign, so their means are
# +/-0.095; one uncompensated decision moves a window's mean by 1e-2, so
# 3e-3 holds the digit density to a third of a decision per half period.
